label: input token b at original position >= 4
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase when the input token is b and the position is t >= 4 (fifth original token or later). It never fires at t = 0..3, at the delimiter, or in the copy phase (including copy-phase b inputs), and essentially never on any other token (~40 stray activations out of 41k). Magnitude rises steadily with absolute position: about 0.13-0.16 of max at t=4, ~0.44 at t=5, ~0.64 at t=6, ~0.78 at t=7, and ~0.97-1.0 at t=8, which is why the top examples are all b as the 9th token. Position t, not tokens-remaining, sets magnitude: t=5 gives ~0.44 whether 1 or 3 tokens remain. Prior tokens, first token, digit count and repeats have no noticeable effect. Dev: precision 1.0, recall 0.999.

issues: No refuting evidence found. On test, the predicate gets precision 1.0 (0 false positives), recall 0.9986 and mass recall 0.99995. Coverage by activation quartile is 0.995 / 1 / 1 / 1.

The 56 test misses are scattered and tiny: activations of 0.01-0.02 of the max, 0.0% of the activation mass, all at step 8 on assorted non-b tokens (g, l, f, u, i, p, w, h). This is noise, not a systematic class.

The phase claims check out on the dev profile: 0 activations at the delimiter and in the copy phase (2.73M copy steps), so b fed back as a copy input never fires. The t=0..3 claim also holds: 0 activations at each.

The magnitude ramp matches the dev examples: about 0.11-0.16 at t=4, 0.44-0.45 at t=5, 0.64 at t=6 and 0.78 at t=7. All top examples are b at t=8 at 0.97-1.0. Activation rate per orig_idx is a flat 0.033-0.034 for t=4..8, consistent with every b firing there.

Minor caveat: the claim that 'previous tokens have no visible effect' is supported only by flat prev_tok and first_tok rates and a few examples, e.g. b at t=6 after an earlier b at t=4 still gives 0.64. Nothing contradicts it.
